findings.reason: the honest change is a new phase in the existing engine, and §7's own text already leans on workers.py's pattern, so it should use the owner rather than copy it.
findings.text: §7 places the candidate claim loop in a new imas_codex/ids/candidate_workers.py, but the SignalSource claim machinery is already owned by imas_codex/ids/workers.py: claim_sources_for_mapping at :198, release_mapping_claim at :274, has_pending_mapping_work at :329, and the phase/orphan-recovery wiring in run_mapping_engine at :903 with orphan_specs at :972 — all keyed on SignalSource.mapping_claim_token. A second claim loop over the same node type, the same @retry_on_deadlock + ORDER BY rand() + claim-token pattern and the same orphan recovery path will drift from this, and §6 already adds candidate_claim_token/candidate_status to the same SignalSource the workers.py claim queries read — the plan should extend workers.py (add a claim function and a phase there) rather than fork the loop

findings.reason: naming the owner (tools/graph_search.py) redirects §4's fix and forces a decision about the two superseded entry points; §4 already claims to add no parallel owner.
findings.text: §4 moves cluster expansion out of gather_ids_context and fixes the K-hits defect in compute_semantic_matches (imas_codex/ids/tools.py:769), and each is the legacy path: the module docstring at imas_codex/tools/graph_search.py:1 declares GraphSearchTool "replaces DocumentStore, SemanticSearch, and ClusterSearcher", search_imas_semantic (imas_codex/ids/tools.py:114) already delegates to GraphSearchTool.search_dd_paths, and imas_codex/graph/dd_search.py:869 exposes cluster_search — yet §4 names only ClusterSearcher (imas_codex/clusters/search.py:92) and compute_semantic_matches, measured as the "today" arm in §3. Fixing K-hits after the category filter (the LIMIT-in-SEARCH / WHERE-category pattern §3 describes) in the legacy function leaves the defect in the maintained owner; the plan should extend GraphSearchTool.search_dd_paths, and say whether compute_semantic_matches is retired once §4 lands

findings.reason: the section must account for the surface it adds under the interface-budget rule, naming what it retires or why nothing can be, before the CLI is built.
findings.text: §7 adds `imas-codex discover map` with seven options (--physics-domain/-d, --ids/-i, --cost-limit/-c, --time, --limit, --rejudge, --dry-run) to the cli_options family, whose supplied count is 0, and neither §7 nor §8 states whether any existing `imas map` sub-option is retired or merged, or why the option set cannot reuse discover signals' existing flags verbatim

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — imas_codex/ids/candidates.py hides vector retrieval, cluster expansion, the unit filter, deduplication and candidate metadata assembly behind one function returning dict[str, list[Candidate]]; that is depth behind a small interface, not a spread of wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §7 adds a new candidate_workers.py claim loop beside the module that already owns SignalSource claiming and orphan recovery.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §7 adds a new subcommand with seven CLI options and names nothing it retires or merges, nor why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched and cites real mechanisms: compute_semantic_matches (imas_codex/ids/tools.py:769), analyze_units (imas_codex/ids/tools.py:168, whose dimensionality check §4 correctly reuses), ClusterSearcher (imas_codex/clusters/search.py:92), fetch_cross_facility_mappings (imas_codex/ids/tools.py:733), the jt60sa §25 call_decisions layer it defers to, run_jev_v3.py's facility block, get_triage_threshold (imas_codex/settings.py:1009) and the shared DiscoveryConfig/run_discovery harness (imas_codex/cli/discover/common.py); I opened each and found it.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no proposed module merely forwards to existing machinery without adding behaviour: candidates.py composes three arms with dedup and scoring, judgment.py builds the decisions state and adds route(), write_candidates adds a count-check that raises, and §5 explicitly states it calls the shared decisions layer and builds no second client.
